children: U.S. equities closed lower Wednesday as Treasury yields spiked, all while President Trump raised the prospect of a negotiated end to the U.S. conflict with Iran.
The blue-chip Dow
ended lower by -0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) handed back -0.8%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
lost -1.1%.
From a sector-by-sector stance, just one of the 11 segments closed higher, and that was energy as oil
advanced more than 2%. At the other end of the spectrum, communication services struggled the most.

“It makes sense for the market to pull back some after hitting a fresh high. After all, the euphoria eventually has to ease. However, the decline was not just because of this. It was also because of other issues. For instance, the market is increasingly concerned that the Federal Reserve is going to hike interest rates at least one more time before this year is out. But also, U.S. Treasuries have continued to become more expensive,” Seeking Alpha analyst
stated.

Over on the geopolitical front, President Trump addressed the United Nations on Tuesday and said he expects the United States eventually to reach an agreement with Iran. He said he believes Tehran will make a deal after the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3.
Treasury yields
higher on the session. The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield
climbed 14 basis points to 4.89%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield
moved higher by 15 basis points to 5.10%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield
pushed up 10 basis points to 5.39%.
Moreover, the U.S. Treasury's $70B five-year note (US5Y) auction on Wednesday met with lackluster demand, with market participants demanding the highest yield since 2006.
As for stocks that were on the move, shares of CrowdStrike
advanced +4.9%, while shares of Paychex
fell -8.7%.

title: U.S. equities closed deep in the red while Treasury yields surged
